root_cause.text: In `drm/vmwgfx`’s `vmw_kms_fb_create()` path, the code unconditionally called `surface->res.func->dirty_alloc(&surface->res)` for KMS surfaces even when `surface->res.dirty` was already set, overwriting the existing dirty tracker and leaking the previously allocated tracker object.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `vmw_kms_fb_create()` from `ret = surface->res.func->dirty_alloc(&surface->res);` to `if (surface->res.dirty == NULL) ret = surface->res.func->dirty_alloc(&surface->res);`, and the commit message explicitly says “We were overwriting the surface's dirty tracker here causing a memory leak.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid reinitializing dirty tracking for surfaces that already have a dirty object in vmw_kms_fb_create().
intent_record.what: In vmw_kms_fb_create(), the call to surface->res.func->dirty_alloc(&surface->res) is now wrapped in a check that only invokes it when surface->res.dirty is NULL; the existing assignment surface->res.coherent = true remains unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents dirty_alloc from being called again for a surface resource that already has a dirty object attached, avoiding redundant allocation or reinitialization of dirty tracking while still marking the resource coherent when appropriate.

grouping_result.intent: Avoid reinitializing dirty tracking for surfaces that already have a dirty object in vmw_kms_fb_create().

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it prevents vmw_kms_fb_create() from calling dirty_alloc again when a dirty tracker already exists, avoiding overwriting and leaking the existing tracker.

candidates.rationale: This is the unconditional dirty-tracker allocation call in vmw_kms_fb_create() that overwrites any existing dirty object for KMS surfaces, which matches the root cause of leaking the previously allocated tracker.

vuln_statements.explanation: This unconditional allocation call in vmw_kms_fb_create() reinitializes the dirty tracker even when surface->res.dirty is already set, which overwrites the existing tracker and leaks the previously allocated object.

commit d9186faeae6efb7d0841a5e8eb213ff4c7966614
Author: Ian Forbes <ian.forbes@broadcom.com>
Date:   Fri Nov 14 14:37:03 2025 -0600

    drm/vmwgfx: Fix KMS with 3D on HW version 10
    
    HW version 10 does not have GB Surfaces so there is no backing buffer for
    surface backed FBs. This would result in a nullptr dereference and crash
    the driver causing a black screen.
    
    Fixes: 965544150d1c ("drm/vmwgfx: Refactor cursor handling")
    Signed-off-by: Ian Forbes <ian.forbes@broadco
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is the unconditional call to `surface->res.func->dirty_alloc(&surface->res)` when a KMS surface already has a dirty tracker. In this snippet, that exact path is no longer unconditional: the code now wraps the BO dirty/dirty_alloc sequence in `if (bo) { ... if (!ret && surface && surface->res.func->dirty_alloc) { ... ret = surface->res.func->dirty_alloc(&surface->res); } ... }`. This means the shown function no longer blindly allocates a dirty tracker for every KMS surface; it only does so when `bo` exists and after `vmw_bo_dirty_add(bo)` succeeds. Therefore the previously described leak-causing construct is absent here, and the fix is already present in this commit snippet.
